name: Zijin Cloud Big Data Center
developer: Gansu Zijin Cloud Big Data Development / Gansu Energy Investment; China Telecom partnership for Tianyi Cloud facility
notes: Green Data Center recognition article says the project is a Gansu 13th Five-Year key information project, planned in three phases with about CNY5.0bn investment; phase 1 first stage had 2,543 rentable racks and a telecom business license. DCD/IDCNova reported a China Telecom Tianyi Cloud Big Data Center inaugurated at the Zijin Cloud site with 203 initial racks and 260 servers.

name: Gansu Jiuquan Cloud Computing Big Data Center
developer: Jiuquan municipal project; tenants include Inspur Group, Shanghai Newtouch, Tianhe Cloud
notes: Opened April 28, 2021. Reported as a 100-mu, CNY3.0bn, three-phase cloud-computing/big-data center with 10,000 planned racks; phase 1 completed with 18,300 sqm and 2,200 standard racks in operation.

name: China Mobile (Gansu Lanzhou) Data Center Phase II / Lanzhou New Area Data Center
developer: China Mobile Group Gansu Co., Ltd.; contractor China Construction Third Engineering Bureau
notes: CSCEC reported phase II passed completion acceptance in Lanzhou New Area, adding one data-center building and one power center across about 26,000 sqm with about 7,000-rack installed capacity; Uptime lists the China Mobile Gansu Lanzhou New Area Data Center Phase 1 floor.

name: Lanzhou New Area Big Data Industrial Park IDC facilities
developer: Lanzhou New Area Science, Culture and Tourism Group with China Mobile, ZTE, Huawei, Sugon and other partners
notes: China Belt and Road portal reported Lanzhou New Area had landed China Mobile, China Telecom, State Grid cloud data centers plus Huawei and Sugon projects; 1# IDC, smart-city operations center, power building and R&D building were operating, with phase II under construction and about 15,200 racks available after completion.

name: Linxia Prefecture Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Linxia Prefecture, China Mobile Gansu, CHN Energy Gansu Power, Beijing Zhongshu Botong Technology
notes: Framework agreement signed September 13, 2024. Planned investment CNY1.5bn, including AI compute, storage, network and operations platforms; total planned computing capacity 3,000 PFLOPS.

name: Wujiu Expressway modular data centers
developer: Gansu Changda Road Industry / Gansu Provincial Highway Aviation Tourism Investment Group; Huawei Digital Power solution
notes: Huawei case study describes a distributed transport-infrastructure data center deployment for the Wujiu Expressway in Longnan: 11 toll/service/tunnel sites use FusionModule800 micro-modular data centers, with the monitoring sub-center using FusionModule2000, deployed within one month. Small edge/special-purpose facility rather than public colocation.

name: Gansu Qingyang National Data Center Cluster / East-Data-West-Computing Industrial Park
developer: Qingyang East Data West Computing Industrial Park / Qingyang Yunchuang Smart Big Data Co., Ltd.; multiple telecom and AI tenants
notes: NDRC identified Gansu/Ningxia as a national computing hub. AIIB lists a proposed USD410m green/low-carbon infrastructure project supporting expansion of Qingyang Computing Industrial Park. People's Daily reported 6 intelligent-computing centers operational, 10+ under construction, 31,000 racks operating and more than 51,000 PFLOPS. National Data Administration/CCTV later reported about 22 data-center buildings planned to start in 2026 and a target above 200,000 PFLOPS by year-end.

name: China Mobile (Gansu Qingyang) Data Center N01 / New Industrialization Green Intelligent Computing Center
developer: China Mobile Group Gansu Co., Ltd.
notes: People's Daily identified the China Mobile new industrialization green intelligent computing center inside Qingyang EDWC park as operational. Science and Technology Daily described China Mobile (Gansu Qingyang) Data Center N01 as Gansu's first 18 kW intelligent-computing high-power data center and part of a domestic 10,000-card compute cluster.

name: China Telecom Gansu Qingyang Intelligent Computing Center
notes: Gansu press reported China Telecom Gansu Qingyang Intelligent Computing Center started construction in 2024 as part of the Qingyang cluster. People's Daily later described the China Telecom Qingyang computing center's Xirang scheduling platform operating with more than 30,000 PFLOPS visible in the dispatch platform.

name: Northwest Zero-Carbon Smart Cloud Intelligent Computing Center Phase I
notes: Phase I started construction February 28, 2026 in Qingyang East-Data-West-Computing Industrial Park. Reported investment CNY2.585bn, site area 58.33 mu, nearly 90,000 sqm, two machine-room buildings plus power building, 6,600 high-density racks and planned compute above 30,000-35,000 PFLOPS with PUE <=1.198.

name: Gansu Mobile Second Big Data Center
notes: C114/People's Posts and Telecommunications News reported a groundbreaking in Tianshui Chengji New City: CNY350m investment, 20-mu site and 1,000 racks. Later Tianshui government/technology-bureau snippets describe the Gansu Mobile Second Big Data Center as built; operational status inferred from those later public government references.

name: Daosheng Cloud (Wuwei) Intelligent Computing Center
developer: Daosheng Cloud (Wuwei) Digital Technology Co., Ltd.
notes: T1 building lit up on December 31, 2024; Gansu Daily reported the Hexi area's first large-scale AI computing facility entered operation. Site is 172 mu, about CNY5.0bn investment, about 140,000 sqm gross floor area, 4 high-performance computing buildings, 25,000 PFLOPS total planned floating-point compute, with initial 1,000 PFLOPS domestic inference compute and 5,000 PFLOPS capacity in T1.
